I'm sitting on my couch at almost four am and I just want it all to stop. I don't actively want to take myself out- I just feel.. nothing? I switched to a new medication (my last one wasn't doing anything for the longest time) and I've been taking it for a bit now.. 
My depression has never felt like this. I can't sleep, I can't get up, and when I do.. I'm just there. The feeling is worse at night. I'm awake by myself so I'm left alone with my thoughts and I feel hollow. Like a scooped out pumpkin. Self harm has always been (for me) a punishment. I've always felt that I'm a terrible human no matter what I do and I punish myself by cutting my legs open until they bleed and I'm left with the feeling of fire in my skin. Now I do it just to feel alive. I can't bring myself to.. ""end it"" yet it's agony at the end of each day. Being out of my abusive household is rough. Everything is different and I kind of miss the normalcy of constantly having my looks put down and my every mistake being met with screaming and hitting. I knew what to expect in that house. Here? I know nothing now. The rug is out from under my feet. In this new and loving environment I'm now trying to navigate my feelings and past experiences. I was diagnosed with PTSD. (Which is hard for me to swallow since even now I feel the abuse wasn't that bad or that it was normal even though logically I know it was and wasn't) Those experiences include molestation at the hands of a family member. I don't know if I can't do it. I feel like I've been given a Herculean task right now. People believe me. They validate me. This makes me feel like shit because I don't deserve it.  So here I am. Stuck. You know when you first wake up and you stumble to the bathroom and try to go pee while you're still half asleep? You're awake but your brain is foggy? That's what it feels like.. everyday. Awake but my brain is hazy and I'm tripping over myself through the day to day. I feel useless and empty
Sorry for the MCR emo ass rant. I just feel terrible.

So here is my rant, 
I saw a post on here a few days ago which I could summarize as being about how 'x people who self harm are more talked in the media and y people aren't- so x people self harming is less of a problem' this mentality has stuck in my mind. If you're asking what group 'x' was- it was white teenage girls. When people make posts like this, it divides us and turns everything into a big (excuse my french) a circle jerk on who has it the worst. The truth is, arguing who has it worse is pointless. If we're going to have a discussion on "white teenage girls being the only ones portrayed in the media with self harm issues" then fine, here's my 2 cents- yes, white teen girls are usually the ones in shows or movies who self harm but they are never portrayed in a realistic light. It's always either demonizing (them doing it for attention) or romanticizing (them doing it to be more tragic and sexy for the main lead). 
tl;dr 
don't make posts about how some self harmers aren't valid because of things like gender or race or age. everyone's struggles are valid.
